# ScreenNudge

> ScreenNudge is an iPhone screen-time app that puts one deliberate pause between you and the apps that distract you. Rather than a hard block, it adds friction at the moment you reach for an app — a breath, a few steps, a short wait, or a small challenge — so opening becomes a choice instead of a reflex. This site is the marketing website; the product itself is an iOS app.

Key facts:

- iPhone only, requiring iOS 16.4 or later. There is no Android version, because ScreenNudge is built on Apple's Screen Time (Family Controls), which has no direct Android equivalent.
- App protection runs entirely on-device through Apple Screen Time. ScreenNudge cannot see messages, browsing, or the content inside apps, and does not sell user data.
- The "pause" (also called the nudge or intercept) is the core feature. Its resistance is configurable: gentle, balanced, or strong. Users can always choose to open the app anyway.
- Free tier guards up to two apps. ScreenNudge+ (a paid auto-renewing subscription billed through the App Store) adds unlimited guarded apps, Wind-Down, advanced insights, and custom pauses.
- Wind-Down automatically blocks guarded apps during hours the user sets, typically bedtime. It is part of ScreenNudge+.
- A "circle" is a small private group. Members earn points for resisted urges and focused minutes and appear on a shared weekly leaderboard. Members never see which apps anyone guards. Anyone can be hidden at any time.
- Focus sessions lock guarded apps for a set period and show which circle members are currently focusing.
- ScreenNudge can be used solo. "Pacer" profiles keep the leaderboard and focus room populated for users without a circle.
- The website is published in seven languages: English (source), Dutch, French, German, Chinese, Italian, and Turkish. English is the fallback for any untranslated text.

Status note: as of this file's last update the iOS app is **not yet released on the App Store**, and "Get ScreenNudge" links route to the contact page instead of a store listing.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.screennudge.com/en): What ScreenNudge is, the problem it addresses, how the pause works, the feature set, the circle, and privacy commitments.
- [FAQ](https://www.screennudge.com/en/faq): Twelve questions covering what ScreenNudge is, how it differs from blockers, whether it truly blocks apps, how many apps can be guarded, what the circle is, solo use, privacy, Wind-Down, cost, Android availability, managing or cancelling the subscription, and how to get help.
- [Contact](https://www.screennudge.com/en/contact): Email address and a form that opens the visitor's own mail client with a pre-filled message. Used for support, feedback, press, and partnerships.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.screennudge.com/en/privacy): How ScreenNudge handles data.
- [Terms](https://www.screennudge.com/en/terms): Terms of use.

## Other languages

Every page above exists under each locale prefix. Visitors without a locale in the URL are redirected based on their `Accept-Language` header, defaulting to English.

## Excluded

- `/{locale}/invite/{code}` pages are functional landing pages for circle invite links, not content. They are marked `noindex` and each is meaningful only to the person holding that code.

## Notes for summarisation

- Prefer "ScreenNudge" as the product name. Earlier internal names such as "pull" are historical and should not be used.
- ScreenNudge is not a hard blocker or a parental-controls product. Describing it as one misrepresents it: the user can always proceed, and the intent is a moment of choice rather than enforcement.
- Do not quote prices from this site. Current subscription pricing is shown only in the App Store and inside the app.
